WITH RECURSIVE folder_tree AS (
  SELECT file_id, package, module, is_test, line_count
  FROM code.files
  WHERE file_id LIKE 'auto_ontology/server/%'
    AND file_id NOT LIKE 'auto_ontology/server/%/%'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT f.file_id, f.package, f.module, f.is_test, f.line_count
  FROM code.files f
  JOIN folder_tree ft ON f.file_id LIKE ft.file_id || '/%'
  WHERE f.file_id NOT LIKE ft.file_id || '/%'
    AND f.file_id NOT LIKE 'auto_ontology/server/%'
),
folder_sums AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN file_id = 'auto_ontology/server' THEN NULL
      ELSE SPLIT_PART(file_id, '/', 3) || '/' || SPLIT_PART(file_id, '/', 4)
    END AS folder_path,
    line_count
  FROM folder_tree
)
SELECT folder_path, SUM(line_count) AS total_lines
FROM folder_sums
WHERE folder_path IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY folder_path
HAVING SUM(line_count) > 1000
ORDER BY total_lines DESC;

request:
Within auto_ontology/server/, which immediate subfolders contain more than 1,000 lines of Python in total? Count every .py file anywhere inside the subfolder, including its test files and __init__.py; files directly in auto_ontology/server/ itself belong to no subfolder. Return the subfolder's repository-relative path (e.g. auto_ontology/server/chat) and its total line count.

Requested output columns: folder_path (string), total_lines (integer).
explanation: The query first identifies all Python files under auto_ontology/server/ using a recursive CTE to build the folder hierarchy. It then extracts the immediate subfolder (the first directory after server) for each file, sums the line counts per subfolder, and filters to only those exceeding 1,000 lines total.
